Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

it’s time to … phrase

also it’s time, time to, time to get up, it’s time to get up, time for bed, it’s time for

classical

Liv. 21.54.2: nunc corpora cūrāre tempus est
Cic. Top. 1.5: sed jam tempus est ad id quod īnstituimus accēdere (Lewis & Short s.v. tempus)
Traupman 35: tempus est surgere

tempus est (+ infinitive)

tempus est with an infinitive; the person, if named, as subject accusative or dative

English “it’s time to” goes word for word: tempus est surgere, it’s time to get up. With a person: tempus est mē abīre (Cic. Tusc. 1.99) or tibi abīre (Hor. Epist. 2.2.215).

Other words

  • tempus est (+ genitive) — it’s time for …

    tempus est with the genitive of a noun or gerund · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 122.9: lūcet: somnī tempus est

    “Time for sleep”, “time for supper”: the thing in the genitive.

Examples

  • Tempus est surgere.

    It’s time to get up.Traupman 35

  • nunc corpora cūrāre tempus est

    now it is time to look after ourselves (food, a bath, rest)Liv. 21.54.2

  • lūcet: somnī tempus est.

    it’s getting light: time for bed!Sen. Ep. 122.9

See also it’s time to sleep, be awake, get up, I must go.
